authorReviewNote: Top Gear is the BBC programme with Clarkson, Hammond and May. The Grand Tour shared those presenters but was not a BBC programme; Fifth Gear and Wheeler Dealers do not match. Actual Clarkson lead/career passages inspected. The broadcaster qualifier makes the offered answer unique.

Eurovision Song Contest is Norton's BBC television commentary role, explicitly described in the biography. The X Factor, The Voice and Britain's Got Talent do not match that role. Commentary is distinguished from general entertainment hosting; no current broadcast schedule is asserted.

Strictly Come Dancing is the programme Winkleman co-presented with Tess Daly. Actual 2010 results-show and 2014 main-show passages inspected. She also presented So You Think You Can Dance, but not as the regular duo with Daly. Replaced the existing Traitors-host duplicate; historical wording avoids a current-host claim.

Taskmaster was created by Alex Horne. Actual lead explicitly names the creator and assistant roles. Would I Lie to You?, Mock the Week and 8 Out of 10 Cats are other programmes. Existing assistant-identification question tests a different fact; guest appearances do not imply creation.

Drama was Davies's school subject. Actual paragraph describes thirteen years as a secondary-school drama teacher. Mathematics, chemistry and geography do not match. Full-time-comedian wording avoids suggesting he could never perform comedy while still teaching; English studied at university is not offered as a false alternative.

Jo Brand worked as a nurse before her professional comedy career. Actual lead explicitly describes the move from psychiatric nursing into alternative stand-up. Architect, journalist and accountant do not match that documented earlier career. No claim that she never wrote journalism later.

Ranganathan taught mathematics at Hazelwick and Beacon, according to the actual career paragraph inspected. History, chemistry and music are not his documented teaching subject. He performed comedy while teaching, so the final question correctly specifies becoming a full-time comedian.

Lee Mack began hosting the UK 1% Club in 2022, as stated in the actual biography. Rob Brydon, Alan Carr and David Mitchell do not match. Original UK version and year avoid confusing international adaptations or later guest appearances.

McIntyre was the original BBC Wheel host. Actual career paragraph explicitly says he began the new BBC game show in November 2020; the US version came later. Greg Davies, Lee Mack and Rob Brydon do not match the launch role. Fixed historical role, not a prediction about future hosts.

Grand Designs debuted in 1999 with McCloud, explicitly stated in the actual lead. Homes Under the Hammer, DIY SOS and Location, Location, Location are other property programmes. Debut wording avoids relying on an indefinitely current presenting contract.

Clarke trained as an architect, not chef, veterinarian or accountant. Correct television-presenter biography and actual architectural qualifications paragraph inspected; Newcastle's own graduate profile also corroborated the training. Initial architect URL returned disambiguation and was rejected. No confusion with McCloud's different educational background.

DIY SOS is Knowles's home-renovation presenting programme, listed in the actual lead. Grand Designs, Homes Under the Hammer and Location, Location, Location have different established presenting associations. Question concerns his recognised programme, not possible guest appearances on other shows.

Bruce became Question Time's presenter in 2019, explicitly stated in the actual lead. Raworth, Maitlis and Wark are other news broadcasters, not the appointee. Historical date avoids any claim about an unchanged future presenter.

Antiques is Dickinson's expert field, supported by the actual antiques-dealer and television-career passages. Wildlife, gardening and motoring do not match his principal television expertise. Does not imply he has no other personal interests.

Osman created the Thursday Murder Club novels. Actual author/series passages inspected. The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency, Jack Reacher and Cormoran Strike are series by other authors. No confusion with Osman's television quiz work or his musician brother.

QI passed from Stephen Fry to Toksvig in 2016, explicitly stated in the actual biography. Would I Lie to You?, Mock the Week and Have I Got News for You do not match that succession. Does not ask which programme she currently presents or confuse guest appearances with hosting.

Raducanu won the 2021 US Open, stated in the actual lead. Wimbledon, Australian Open and French Open are the other offered singles majors, not that victory. Fixed result; no current ranking, record status or future career-total claim.

Gauff became a tennis star. Actual biography identifies her professional sport directly. Golf, basketball and athletics do not match. Broad professional recognition makes this accessible; no changing title total or ranking used.

Osaka is professionally associated with tennis, not badminton, table tennis or squash. Actual lead identifies her sport. Other racket sports are plausible alternatives, but no implication that she could never play them recreationally. Nationality and residence are not confused.

Ainslie's Olympic gold medals were in sailing, not rowing, canoeing or swimming. Actual lead describes Olympic sailing results. No current team ownership, employment or claim about his still being the most successful sailor is needed.

Daley's Olympic gold was in diving. Actual biography identifies the synchronised platform title. Swimming, water polo and rowing are other sports; broad aquatic connection does not make swimming the medal discipline. No calendar-year ambiguity about the postponed Tokyo Games.

Breaststroke is Peaty's documented specialism. Actual sprint-breaststroke lead inspected. Backstroke, butterfly and freestyle do not match his best-known events. Does not claim he is physically unable to swim other strokes or use a changing world record.

Adlington won Olympic freestyle events, explicitly 400m and 800m in the actual biography. Breaststroke, backstroke and butterfly do not match those events. Question asks event type rather than asserting freestyle rules require a single physical stroke.

Jones won those Olympic titles in taekwondo, stated in the actual lead. Boxing is a later career, so Olympic years are essential; judo and fencing do not match. Avoided a misleading present-tense question that could make boxing and taekwondo both defensible.

Adams's Olympic championship sport was boxing, not judo, taekwondo or wrestling. Actual biography's London/Rio boxing titles inspected. Does not rely on changing professional records or confuse entertainment appearances with her sporting medals.

Taylor won Ireland's London 2012 boxing gold. Actual Olympic career paragraphs inspected. Judo, taekwondo and fencing do not match. Her separate football career is not offered as a false alternative; no current retirement or title-count claim.

Biles is famous for Olympic gymnastics, not diving, athletics or swimming. Actual artistic-gymnast biography lead inspected. Does not mix artistic and rhythmic gymnastics as competing answers or use changing medal totals.

Pommel horse was Whitlock's gold apparatus at both named Olympic editions. Actual lead/Rio and Tokyo paragraphs checked. Parallel bars, horizontal bar and rings do not match. Edition wording matters because Tokyo 2020 took place in 2021; floor exercise is not a false alternative because he also won that in Rio.

Simmonds won Paralympic swimming golds, supported by the actual S6 swimming biography. Athletics, cycling and archery do not match. Correctly says Paralympic rather than Olympic; no unnecessary age, classification detail or changing record.

Cockroft is known for wheelchair racing, explicitly stated in the actual lead. Wheelchair tennis, swimming and archery are different activities. Wording does not incorrectly require wheelchair racing to be a separately named top-level Paralympic sport rather than an athletics discipline.

O'Sullivan's main professional cue sport is snooker. Actual lead inspected. Pool, carom billiards and English billiards are not his defining championship career. Best-known scope does not claim he has never played another cue game.

Littler's sport is darts and his nickname is The Nuke, both explicit in the actual biography. Snooker, boxing and tennis do not match that person. No current world ranking, age record or title total used.

Humphries is Cool Hand, not Littler, Price or van Gerwen. Actual lead explicitly gives the nickname. Cool Hand Luke is a longer variant, not offered as a competing answer; other choices are distinct darts players.

Trump became world champion in snooker. Actual lead/career passages inspected. Pool, English billiards and carom billiards do not match the world title; participation in a pool event is not the same as winning its world championship. Historical achievement, no present ranking claim.

Cavendish's sport is cycling, not motor racing, rowing or marathon running. Actual biography describes both track and road careers. Cycling is intentionally broad; track and road are not offered as mutually exclusive answers when both would be true.

Hoy won his Olympic golds in track cycling. Actual lead states track cyclist and racing driver; the Olympic qualifier excludes his separate motor-racing career. Rowing, sailing and track athletics do not match. No all-time-record claim.

Ma is a cellist, directly stated in the actual lead and training paragraphs. Violin, harp and flute do not match his principal instrument. No birth-country versus nationality confusion or changing award total.

Lang Lang is a classical pianist, directly stated in the actual lead. Cello, trumpet and harp do not match. Question does not claim he still judges The Piano, a role the biography says he left after its first two series.

Benedetti is a violinist, explicitly stated in the actual lead. Cello, double bass and harp do not match. Her separate festival-director role and changing appointments do not affect this stable instrument fact.

Balsom is known for trumpet, explicitly stated in the actual lead and lessons paragraph. Oboe, flute and saxophone do not match. Past/public recognition wording remains true after retirement; no current-performance schedule claim.
